title: Sell Mineral Rights in Antler, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Antler, ND
metaDescription: Antler sits near Bottineau County's old Newburg-era oil fields close to the Canadian border. See what that legacy history means for a mineral interest there.
heroLead: Antler sits close to the Canadian border in Bottineau County, near the older Newburg-area conventional fields that put this part of the state on the map decades before the modern Bakken boom.
intro: Families holding minerals near Antler often have interests tied to that earlier conventional era, wells drilled into the Madison group back in the 1950s and 60s, rather than to modern horizontal Bakken development. Those older wells, where still producing, tend to run at low, steady stripper rates rather than the higher early-life volumes typical of a new well.

sections.heading: Antler's Ties to the Older Newburg-Era Fields
paragraphs: The Newburg and Wiley fields, discovered in the 1950s, sit near Antler and represent Bottineau County's original oil boom, decades before horizontal drilling reached this part of the basin.

sections.heading: What a Legacy Well Near Antler Typically Produces
paragraphs: Where these older wells still produce, output is generally low and steady rather than sharply declining, which shows up as a modest, fairly consistent royalty check month to month rather than the higher, faster-declining pattern of a new Bakken well.

sections.heading: Confirming Your Interest
paragraphs: The Bottineau County Recorder's office in Bottineau holds the deed and probate chain for Antler-area tracts, and because production here has run for decades, that paper trail is often longer than in newer development areas.

sections.heading: What to Expect From an Antler-Area Review
paragraphs: Given the older, steady nature of production near the historic Newburg field, we typically find Antler-area interests easier to value with confidence once current production is confirmed, since the output pattern tends to be more predictable than newer, faster-declining Bakken wells.

faqs.question: Is Antler near the historic Newburg oil field?
faqs.answer: Yes, Antler sits close to the Newburg and Wiley fields, discovered in the 1950s, which represent Bottineau County's original conventional oil boom.

faqs.question: Why is my Antler-area royalty check so consistent month to month?
faqs.answer: Older conventional wells in this area typically produce at low, steady stripper rates rather than the faster decline pattern of a newer Bakken well, which shows up as a more consistent check.

faqs.question: Where do I find Antler mineral records?
faqs.answer: The Bottineau County Recorder's office in Bottineau holds deed and probate records, often going back decades given the area's older production history.

faqs.question: Is my Antler mineral interest still worth something if the well is old?
faqs.answer: Yes, a well several decades into production can still generate steady value, and we evaluate current production rather than assuming an older well means less value.

faqs.question: Is legacy production near Antler more predictable to value than newer Bakken wells?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, steady stripper-rate production is easier to project forward than a new well still in its early decline phase, which can make valuation more straightforward.
